author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Vita3K adds a second keyboard binding to every mapped action
summary: The controls dialog, configuration schema, axis synthesis, Vita buttons, and emulator shortcuts now treat either of two scancodes as the same action.
heroAlt: Source evidence from Vita3K pull request #3845: Added support for alternate key bindings for keyboard controls

sourceLabels.vita3k-pr-3845: Added support for alternate key bindings for keyboard controls

blocks.text: One key per action is restrictive for real play setups

Players may alternate between laptop and external keyboards, share a machine with different layouts, use both arrow keys and WASD, or need a second ergonomic key for a shoulder button. External remappers can duplicate inputs, but they also affect other applications and hide the relationship from Vita3K's own controls screen. The emulator needs both bindings to participate identically in gameplay and UI shortcuts.
Alternate scancodes are first-class configuration fields

Pull request #3845 adds an -alt setting beside Select, Start, D-pad, face and shoulder buttons, stick clicks, every virtual stick direction, PS button, GUI visibility, fullscreen, touch display, texture replacement, screenshot, pinch modifier, and alternate pinch actions. Defaults use zero for unassigned. The controls table presents a second mapped-button column and capture logic assigns each slot independently using a pointer-based widget ID.
Digital and analog evaluation both accept either key

Button polling checks primary or alternate scancode before setting each Vita bit. keys_to_axis receives two codes for each direction and produces the same negative or positive contribution from either. Event handling for GUI commands, screenshots, texture toggles, and pinch behavior likewise recognizes both fields. This avoids a misleading UI where a second key appears saved but works only in a subset of input paths.
Conflict and release behavior deserve explicit coverage

Bind two keys to one action, one key to several compatible actions, opposite stick directions, primary equal to alternate, and zero as either slot. Hold both keys, release them in different orders, open the remapper during capture, reset mappings, and reload configuration. Exercise gameplay, LiveArea navigation, fullscreen, screenshots, touch and pinch shortcuts. UI feedback should show both assignments clearly, and key-repeat or focus loss must not leave an axis or button stuck.
An alternate binding is useful only when storage, remapping, gameplay polling, virtual axes, and emulator shortcuts all honor it as an equal path.
